jobs.title: Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
At Home Repairs Ministries, a call for help is rarely just about a leaking roof, broken HVAC system, unsafe floor, or plumbing problem. Often, the homeowner on the other end of the phone has been trying to figure out what to do for months—or even years—and doesn’t know where else to turn.
The Program Coordinator is often one of the first people they meet.

This person helps homeowners navigate the process from their first request for assistance through the completion of their repairs. It requires someone who can listen with compassion, communicate clearly, stay exceptionally organized, and make sure people and projects don’t get lost in the process.

But this role is also about building the systems behind that work.

HRM is a growing organization, and we’re looking for someone who can grow with us. The Program Coordinator will help manage the processes, technology, documentation, and workflows that allow our team to serve an increasing number of homeowners.

We’re looking for someone who genuinely cares about people, loves creating order, takes ownership, and sees what needs to happen next.

What You’ll Do

Homeowner Communication & Coordination

Serve as a primary point of contact for homeowners throughout the repair process.
Respond to homeowner calls, emails, and applications with warmth, patience, and professionalism.
Screen applicants for eligibility and collect required documentation.
Schedule home assessments and repair projects with homeowners, Project Managers, contractors, and trade partners.
Keep homeowners informed about project status, next steps, scheduling, and expectations.
Proactively follow up on outstanding information and help keep projects moving from application through completion.

Project & Program Coordination

Coordinate schedules and workflows across multiple homeowners and repair projects.
Track projects, outstanding tasks, deadlines, and next steps.
Prepare project files and assist with estimates, materials, deliveries, and project documentation.
Identify projects that have stalled or need attention and proactively follow up.
Coordinate volunteer opportunities and maintain required volunteer documentation.
Work closely with Project Managers to ensure they have the information and documentation needed to complete their work.
Help develop and improve processes as HRM’s project volume, staff, and programs grow.

Systems, Data & Reporting

The Program Coordinator helps ensure that HRM’s systems reflect what’s actually happening in the field.
Maintain accurate homeowner, project, and program information in Monday.com, Bloomerang, and Google Workspace.
Use Monday.com to actively manage workflows, project status, deadlines, responsibilities, and follow-up.
Maintain accurate records in Bloomerang and other organizational databases.
Identify missing information or documentation and proactively resolve gaps.
Maintain organized and complete homeowner and project files.
Collect and maintain eligibility information, demographics, project costs, photos, completion documentation, outputs, and other information required for grants and government-funded programs.
Work with leadership and grant/compliance staff to ensure program records are complete, timely, and ready for reporting, reimbursement requests, monitoring, or audits.
Support organizational dashboards and monthly, quarterly, and annual program reporting.
Help evaluate and improve systems and workflows as HRM adds programs, funding sources, staff, and project volume.

Who We’re Looking For

This role requires a unique combination of compassion, organization, initiative, and systems thinking.
The right person:
Genuinely enjoys helping people and communicates with warmth and professionalism.
Takes ownership and follows responsibilities through to completion.
Is exceptionally organized and comfortable managing many moving pieces at once.
Naturally asks, “What’s next, what’s missing, and who needs to know?”
Communicates proactively when something changes, stalls, or needs attention.
Has strong attention to detail and understands that accurate documentation matters.
Is comfortable working extensively in technology and database systems.
Can follow established processes while also recognizing when a process could work better.
Is willing to handle the day-to-day details today while having the ability and desire to take on greater operational responsibility as HRM grows.

Qualifications

3+ years of experience in program coordination, project coordination, construction operations, nonprofit administration, office management, or a related field.
Demonstrated ability to manage workflows, multiple projects, schedules, deadlines, and competing priorities.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
Strong technology skills and experience with CRM, project-management, database, or case-management systems.
Strong attention to detail and demonstrated ability to maintain accurate records and documentation.
Experience using Monday.com and/or Bloomerang strongly preferred.
Experience with government-funded programs, grant documentation, compliance, or reporting strongly preferred.
Demonstrated ability to improve processes and create systems that help a team manage increasing volume and complexity.

Benefits

Competitive salary based on experience
Flexible schedule/hybrid
Unlimited PTO
Professional development opportunities
Team environment

How to Apply

This position offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact in the lives of vulnerable homeowners while working within a faith-based dynamic and passionate team. If you are organized, compassionate, and driven to make a difference, we encourage you to apply. Interested candidates should submit their resume and cover letter to info@homerepairs.org.

The Qualified Rehabilitation Consultant (QRC)/Vocational Case Manager provides vocational rehabilitation services and medical case management to individuals following a work place injury through coordination with client, insurer, physician, employer, attorney and others with the ultimate goal being the client’s timely return to gainful employment. The Vocational Case Manager interviews and evaluates the client to determine the degree of disability, eligibility and feasibility of vocational rehabilitation services. This position determines suitable job goals consistent with the clients’ interests, aptitudes and physical limitations; supporting the goals of the Case Management department, and of CorVel.

Candidates with case management experience or vocational rehabilitation background encouraged to apply

This is a Minnesota Field Case Management position. Only MN candidates will be considered.

Essential Functions And Responsibilities

Schedule and carry out appointments with client, family, adjuster, medical providers, employer, attorney, vendors as necessary
Complete forms according to industry requirements
Prepare organized reports within a specified timeframe
Document all case activity in files
Complete ongoing educational requirements as required by certifying entities
May be required to attend committee meetings, participate in customer service activities, present instructional programs, administer vocational testing and review results, perform on-site job analyses, provide expert testimony, job placement, oversee job seeking skills workshop and perform labor market research
Additional duties as required

Knowledge & Skills

Effective multi-tasking skills in a high-volume, fast-paced, team-oriented environment
Ability to interface with claims staff, attorneys, physicians and their representatives, and advisors/clients and coworkers
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Ability to meet designated deadlines
Computer proficiency and technical aptitude with the ability to utilize MS Office including Excel spreadsheets
Strong interpersonal, time management and organizational skills
Ability to work both independently and within a team environment

Education/Experience

Bachelor’s degree or a combination of education and related experience in Rehabilitation Counseling or related field
Qualified Rehabilitation Consultant (QRC) registration with the MN Department of Labor and Industry or ability to obtain
Ability to obtain CRC or CDMS Certification
Knowledge of Managed Care or Workers’ Compensation preferred
RN license or bilingual (Spanish) a plus

Culture Vision at Consumer Direct Care Network

At CDCN, we strive to create a workplace where everyone is supported and motivated to be their best; we collaborate on shared goals and celebrate our accomplishments.

WE WELCOME YOU INTO A GROWING COMPANY

Consumer Direct Care Network is all about caring for people. Care is at our core, and we strive to live up to it every day. We provide services in 14 states across the USA, and our programs grow every year. We specialize in home and community-based services that support individuals with disabilities and older adults so they can remain in their homes and communities.

jobs.description:
The part-time Case Manager provides case management and student support services to adult education students, helping individuals identify and overcome barriers to education, employment, and personal success. Assist students with enrollment, orientation, academic and career planning, referrals to campus and community resources, and ongoing progress monitoring. Build supportive relationships with students, maintain accurate documentation, coordinate with faculty and program staff, and connect students with appropriate resources to promote persistence, completion, and successful transition to employment, postsecondary education, or career training.

This position is part-time, up to 19 hours/week.

Duties And Responsibilities

Commitment to CCRI’s Mission:

Demonstrate a commitment to the philosophy and mission of a comprehensive community college.
Work collaboratively in an inclusive and student-centered environment, with students of various learning styles, cultures, identities, and life-experiences.
Work collaboratively with others and provide quality customer service in an inclusive environment.

Data Management And Administrative Support

Maintain accurate and up-to-date student records, case notes, and program documentation.
Enter and update student information in CRM, student information systems, and other program databases.
Track student enrollment, attendance, participation, academic progress, and program completion.
Monitor student caseloads and maintain organized records of case management activities and follow-up.
Prepare and maintain spreadsheets, reports, rosters, tracking logs, and other administrative documents.
Assist with data collection and reporting requirements for Adult Education programs, grants, and funding sources.

Program Support

Provide direct support to Adult Education students throughout their educational journey.
Assist with student recruitment, intake, enrollment, orientation, and onboarding activities.
Support students in developing educational, career, and personal goals.
Monitor student participation, attendance, progress, and program persistence.
Conduct regular outreach and follow-up with students to encourage engagement and successful program completion.
Connect students with academic, career, workforce, and community resources based on individual needs.
Assist with coordinating student workshops, events, information sessions, and other program activities.
Collaborate with instructors, advisors, staff, and community partners to support student success.
Provide referrals for supportive services, including transportation, childcare, employment, housing, and other community resources, as appropriate.
Help identify barriers that may affect student participation and assist in developing strategies to address those barriers.
Support students in transitioning to postsecondary education, workforce training, credential programs, or employment opportunities.
Participate in program meetings, staff trainings, and professional development activities.
Assist with outreach and communication efforts to promote Adult Education programs and services.
Support special projects and initiatives that enhance student engagement, retention, and completion.
Provide general program and operational support to the Adult Education team as needed.

Student Support

Student Assessment: Meet with students to assess their educational, academic, career, and personal support needs and identify barriers that may impact their success.
Individual Success Planning: Work with students to develop realistic, step-by-step education and career goals, including action plans for enrollment, persistence, and program completion.
Resource Coordination: Connect students with appropriate CCRI resources and community services, including academic support, career services, workforce training, financial resources, transportation, childcare, and other community-based assistance.
Progress Monitoring: Conduct regular check-ins with students to monitor attendance, academic progress, engagement, and progress toward their individual educational and career goals.
Student Advocacy and Support: Advocate for students by helping them navigate college processes, address barriers, communicate with appropriate departments, and access available academic and support services.
Documentation and Data Management: Maintain accurate and confidential records of student contacts, appointments, referrals, case notes, progress updates, and support services in appropriate college databases and digital systems.
Student Crisis and Barrier Support: Assist students in addressing urgent barriers that may interfere with their educational participation and connect them with appropriate CCRI departments, community resources, or emergency services when necessary.

Required Qualifications

Undergraduate or Graduate Degree: Bachelor’s degree in Social Work (BSW), Psychology, Nursing, or Human Services; some residential or entry-level roles accept a High School diploma with relevant experience.
Field Experience: 1 to 3 years of supervised experience in behavioral health, substance use treatment, or social services.
Experience working with adult students
Demonstrated work experience providing outstanding customer service
Demonstrated excellent time management skills, high learning agility, creative problem solving, interpersonal, oral and written communications, and presentation skills, with strong attention to detail and accuracy
Demonstrate proficiency with customer relationships management or data management enterprise software
Demonstrated proficient computer skills including Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, primarily), Google G-Suite and email, Internet applications, and database software
Experience supporting students from diverse backgrounds to engage in education
Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of both assessment and college and/or career readiness curricula for adult students
Knowledge of workforce development services, programs, and /or program providers.
Bilingual skills—Spanish preferred
Knowledge of social and support services available in the community

Midwest Behavioral Health Center is seeking a compassionate, organized, and resourceful Case Manager
to join our multidisciplinary treatment team.
The Case Manager serves as the connection between the care patients receive at MBHC and the people, providers, schools, agencies, and resources that support them outside of treatment. Coordinate Care & Keep Everyone Connected

Required

to oversee data collection, data organization, and/or data management or similar functions/tasks for research studies in support of the PI and Research team.

Run routine and ad hoc reports.

Statistical reasoning.
Competency with Microsoft Word and Excel.
Strong communication skills.
